newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Drought postpones Tanzania's coffee revival plans.
newsitem.headline: Drought postpones Tanzania's coffee revival plans.

text.p: Severe drought affecting much of East Africa has destroyed prospects for a recovery in Tanzania's coffee production for the coming 1997/98 season, an annual industry conference heard on Wednesday.

"The current drought has wiped out the prospects for a quick recovery of production in the coming season," the Coffee Management Unit of Tanzania's agriculture ministry said in a briefing paper at a coffee conference in Moshi.
"We all know that coffee production has declined over the last few years, which is of concern to the entire industry," it added.
From a production peak averaging 55,160 tonnes between 1981 and 1985, the forecast yield for the current 1996/97 season is between 41,000 and 43,000 tonnes worth $95 million.

In his speech at the second annual coffee industry meeting in the northern Tanzanian farming town of Moshi, Agriculture and Cooperative Minister Paul Kamiti acknowledged that "climatic conditions have not been good."
A local farmer told Reuters at the start of the meeting, "Weather is the problem. Flowers are falling off before your very eyes."
Kamiti said industry complaints about excessive taxation and levies were being looked at by a government task force with a view to simplifying the country's taxation system.
Despite the problems, Tanzania's coffee had secured a stable position in the world market with substantial scope for increased exports, he said.

Philip Mbogela, a senior official at the Coffee Management Unit, the government's main policy formulation body, said the emergence of industry newcomers such as Vietnam underscored the need for Tanzania to become more productive and competitive.
"These countries are going to become more competitive. There is only one option. We must become more productive. Our farms must produce more," Mbogela said.
